title: Managed Inference Resilience and Fallback Liability Clause Bank (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
This clause bank is a working set of contract language for negotiating resilience, fallback, and liability allocation related to managed inference services (hosted, dedicated, and private deployments). The goal is to provide interchangeable clause options for commercial teams, legal, and security to accelerate negotiations with customers who require assured continuity of inference service during degradation events, capacity constraints, or region-level outages.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to inference APIs, streaming token services, and managed model endpoints covered under the Agreement.
- Excludes experimental beta features and customer-managed on-prem components unless expressly included.

Key definitions (for clarity in clauses):
- "Primary Service" means the set of inference endpoints, control-plane operations, and related telemetry described in the Order Form.
- "Fallback Mechanism" means any automated or manual measure the Provider operates to maintain application-level availability, including model variant routing, degraded fidelity models, regional routing, or queueing mechanisms.
- "Degraded Response" means a response returned by the Service during which latency, token truncation, model variant, or omission of non-essential features (e.g., tool calling) differs from the Primary Service baseline.
- "Capacity Event" means any event where Provider capacity or routing constraints materially increase request latency or failure rate beyond defined SLOs.
- "Force Majeure" retains its usual contract meaning but does not by default excuse Provider obligations to implement documented fallback mechanisms where those are technically available.

Operational obligations (examples to select from):
- Provider shall maintain a documented Fallback Runbook describing automated routing, model variant hierarchy, and sequence for customer-specific rollouts; Provider shall share a redacted copy with Customer upon execution of a mutual NDA.
- Provider shall implement and keep current an automated model-variant fallback chain that preserves, to the greatest extent feasible, the functional output shape (tokens, structured fields) requested by Customer.
- Provider shall ensure that fallback routes do not cause cross-tenant data leakage and that KV/prefix caches are segregated or flushed per documented procedures when switching model variants or regions.

SLO-backed resilience commitments (select one option during negotiation):
- Option A (Balanced): Provider targets 99.5% availability for inference endpoint responses within the agreed latency band per month. If Availability falls below target due to Capacity Events, Customer receives a service credit equal to percentage of monthly fees attributable to the impacted endpoints pro-rated by downtime.
- Option B (Customer-favorable): Provider guarantees 99.9% endpoint availability and commits to continuous fallback to a specified alternative model family before reverting to error responses. Failure to deliver triggers higher service credits and a right to terminate for material breach after 30 days cure.
- Option C (Provider-favorable): Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain availability and will maintain fallback mechanisms, but SLOs and service credits only apply to non-force-majeure events and subject to documented acceptable usage policies.

Liability allocation and fallback-specific liability language (three variants):
1) Limited Liability (default for Provider):
- Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Provider's aggregate liability for claims arising out of or related to fallback behavior, degraded responses, or model variant selection is limited to the fees paid by Customer for the affected Service in the three (3) months preceding the event. Provider will not be liable for consequential damages resulting from temporary degraded inference output.

2) Balanced Liability (compromise):
- Provider's liability for direct damages caused by willful or grossly negligent misconfiguration of fallback mechanisms is capped at the greater of (a) six (6) months of fees attributable to the affected Service or (b) $1,000,000. Provider remains responsible for implementing documented fallback measures in good faith. Consequential damages remain excluded except where permitted by applicable law.

3) Customer-protective Liability (used for enterprise customers):
- Provider agrees that improper fallback routing that causes data exposure, persistent model hallucination of Customer PII, or a failure to maintain contractual isolation that causes loss to Customer will not be subject to the general limitation of liability; in such cases Provider liability is uncapped up to the proven direct damages.

Service credit formula examples (negotiable):
- Basic: For every 0.1% below the monthly availability target, Customer receives 2% of monthly fees for the affected Service, capped at 100% of that monthly fee.
- Enhanced: For each hour of unmitigated availability below target after Provider's declared initiation of its Fallback Runbook, Customer receives a pro-rated credit equal to (monthly fee / 720) * 200%.

Operational transparency & evidence obligations:
- Provider will maintain incident timelines and post-incident reports for Capacity Events that materially impacted Customer traffic. Customer may request redacted evidence demonstrating fallback actions (routing tables, model ID use, cache flush timestamps) for the affected time window.
- Evidence requests will be subject to Provider's confidentiality obligations and will not require disclosure of Provider proprietary code or low-level performance telemetry beyond what is necessary to corroborate fallback behaviors.

Data handling during fallback and rollbacks:
- All fallback mechanisms shall preserve Customer data handling covenants from the Agreement, including encryption-at-rest and in-transit requirements, no cross-tenant data exposure, and applicable data residency commitments.
- If a fallback route requires routing to a different geographic region, Provider must notify Customer within the incident report and document any legal basis or export control implications.

Audit and compliance: 
- Customer may, at its expense and with reasonable notice (no more than once per 12 months), conduct an audit limited to verifying that fallback processes and data segregation controls operate as documented. Audits may be done by a mutually agreed third party and redacted to protect Provider intellectual property.

Indemnity and remediation obligations (negotiation points):
- Provider will indemnify Customer for third-party claims arising from Provider's gross negligence or willful misconduct in implementing fallback mechanisms that result in data exposure.
- Where fallback leads to known output quality regressions that cause direct contractual losses to Customer (e.g., misrouted payments), Provider will reasonably cooperate on remediation and may provide financial remediation where fault is attributable to Provider configuration decisions.

Termination and transition following repeated fallback failures:
- If Provider experiences more than N Capacity Events in any rolling 12-month period (N to be negotiated; typical values 3–6), and such events materially breached SLOs as set in the Agreement, Customer may (i) terminate for cause after notice and cure period; and (ii) require Provider to support an orderly transition of inference workloads including keys, model artifacts, and a migration runbook.

Insurance and risk transfer:
- Provider is expected to carry cyber and professional liability insurance with limits commensurate with the liability variant selected. Minimum limits should be recorded in the commercial sheet and aligned to the Balanced Liability option or higher for enterprise deals.

Negotiation guide and redlines (practical tips for commercial/legal):
- Commercial teams: map Customer use-cases to the options above. For latency-sensitive customers (real-time chat/support) push for Option B or Balanced Liability. For high-volume background embedding workloads, Option A or Provider-favorable language may be acceptable.
- Security/infra: insist on explicit clauses about cache segmentation, KV eviction behavior during fallbacks, and unacceptable fallback routes (e.g., routing to public/community models).
- Legal: watch for "unlimited" uncapped liability language in Customer-protective drafts — narrow to breaches involving data exposure or willful misconduct.

Draft clause snippets (copy-ready, pick one per section):
- Fallback Runbook Disclosure Snippet: "Provider shall maintain a Fallback Runbook describing automated and manual routing triggers, model variant hierarchy, cache eviction procedures, and escalation contacts. A redacted copy of the Runbook will be made available to Customer under NDA upon request and updated at least semi-annually or upon material change."

- Degraded Response Notice Snippet: "Where Provider returns a Degraded Response pursuant to an implemented Fallback Mechanism, Provider shall include in its response metadata a standardized trace-id and a human-readable reason code. For streaming responses, Provider will prefix the first chunk with the word '[DEGRADED]' and an ISO-8601 timestamp."

- Capacity Event Evidence Snippet: "Upon written request within 60 days of a Capacity Event, Provider will produce redacted routing logs, model-ids, and cache flush records for the impacted timeframe subject to Provider confidentiality obligations. Such requests shall be limited to two per rolling 12 months unless agreed otherwise."

Versioning and change management:
- Provider shall provide 30 days' notice for changes to the fallback hierarchy that may materially affect Customer outputs, with the option for Customer to opt-out of automatic rollout to production for their tenancy for up to 90 days while agreeing to reasonable mitigations.

Open negotiation topics (to be decided on a per-deal basis):
- Definition of "material impact" and quantitative thresholds for what constitutes a Capacity Event.
- Frequency and format of Runbook disclosure and whether security redactions are permitted.
- Whether Fallback Mechanism failures constitute grounds for uncapped liability (limited to specific categories such as data exposure).

Appendix: Example fallback decision tree (textual):
1) Detect latency or error rate > X% for Y minutes -> automatically attempt model-variant #1 (same architecture, smaller quantization) for Z minutes.
2) If model-variant #1 fails to stabilize, route to regional fallback region while preserving customer routing tags and session affinity.
3) If regional fallback unavailable, queue requests for up to Q seconds and return a standardized retryable response.
4) If all fallbacks fail, return a structured error with trace-id and escalate to on-call + notify Customer per the escalation timeline.

Revision notes:
- v0.1 (2025-01-14) initial draft by Avery Chen.
- v0.2 (2025-01-22) added liability variants and evidence snippets (collaborators: Diego Morales, Priya Nair).
- v0.3 (2025-02-02) clarified data handling during cross-region fallback and added runbook notice snippet (Elliot Barnes).

Drafting checklist for deal teams:
- Identify which SLO option will be proposed.
- Confirm runbook disclosure template and NDA terms.
- Map indemnity triggers to specific fallback failure modes.
- Confirm insurance minimums with Risk.

Contact for questions: Avery Chen (avery.chen@redwood.ai) — security-and-compliance.

[End of clause bank draft — editable text for inclusion in DPAs, Master Services Agreements, and Statement of Work exhibits.]
